title: OC Davis Webb on Carolina’s defense: ‘There’ll definitely be some wrinkles’
headline: Webb says Bo Nix is settling in and pushing the ball downfield during Denver's win streak, and rookie RB Jonah Coleman keeps making the most of his chances.
summary: Webb called the offense a 'race to improve' and didn't want to declare it fixed, even with Denver on a winning streak. He said Bo Nix is delivering the ball with conviction and rhythm, trusting his teammates and letting the ball go downfield, and mentioned throws to Jaylen Waddle down the seam and down the left sideline. He praised rookie Jonah Coleman, saying he has shown up every time he's had a chance since rookie minicamp, the preseason, and the games, and that his teammates love him. Webb is 31 and said he is team-first and just wants to win. He seemed to acknowledge that play-calling duties had shifted at some point, but he didn't give details. He warned against overlooking Carolina, citing their high-scoring game against Chicago, their win over Detroit, and last year's playoff near-miss against the Rams. He said Carolina is a couple of plays from a winning record and that there are no cupcakes in the NFL. On Carolina's mid-season coordinator change, he expects the first quarter to be a feeling-out period with new schemes and some banged-up Carolina players. He said there will definitely be some wrinkles, but Denver is ready to attack them. He also said the staff starts self-scouting every Monday and hasn't yet discussed the bye-week plan with Payton.

signals.claim: Nix will keep pushing the ball downfield with confidence and rhythm as the offense continues its run.
signals.note: Webb says Nix is trusting his teammates and throwing downfield, which supports a higher ceiling for Denver's passing game and its pass catchers.
signals.quote: doing a good job really just settling in and trusting his teammates

signals.claim: Coleman will keep earning offensive opportunities and continue to improve as a rookie.
signals.note: Webb's strong praise suggests the rookie has the staff's trust and could see a growing role, though no specific usage was promised.
signals.quote: every time he gets an opportunity, he showed up

topics.detail: Webb avoided declaring the offense fixed, calling it a 'race to improve' while noting Denver is on a winning streak. He said he wants to keep it going and extend the streak to five.

Carolina is under a new coordinator after a mid-season change. Webb expects some wrinkles and a feeling-out first quarter, with banged-up Carolina players a question mark. He compared it to Kansas City's change and said Denver is prepared.
The coaches begin self-scouting every Monday and have done more of it this year. They haven't yet decided with Payton how they'll handle the bye week.

title: Aaron Donald, Puka Nacua & Rams Coordinators speak on playing connected, next-man-up mentality, Week 9 vs. the Commanders & more
headline: Terrance Ferguson is back at practice, which helps 13 personnel. With Davante Adams out, Puka Nacua leads the WRs, and Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington and Konata Mumpfield fill in around him.
summary: Nate Scheelhaase said he was glad to see Terrance Ferguson back on the practice field and moving well, and that the team is excited for him to stack another day. He said the tight end room is deep: Colby Parkinson has made a big impact when healthy, Davis Allen has been consistent, and Tyler Higbee has done well. He praised Tutu Atwell for key plays on conversions and the two-minute drive last week, and said the team wants to get him the ball more, though usage is week to week. He called Puka Nacua a player who always finds a way to make plays, and said he has still been explosive despite the earlier hip and calf injuries. With Davante Adams out, Scheelhaase pointed to Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels as supplements who contribute through blocking and jet sweeps, not just catches. He credited the offense's rhythm in tempo and two-minute situations to continuity among the players. He also spoke warmly about Aaron Donald's mentality and the stories about him around the building. He did not give any game-plan detail for the Commanders.

injuries.detail: Back on the practice field after missing time (listed DNP with an ankle issue on the report). Scheelhaase said he is moving around well and wants him to stack another day.
Referred to as out by the coach and reporters. No timeline was given.
Listed DNP with a knee issue on the report. Scheelhaase spoke only about the earlier hip and calf injuries, saying he is still explosive, and gave no update on the knee.
Listed limited with ribs. Scheelhaase said only that he has made a huge impact when healthy.

signals.claim: Ferguson is back practicing and is expected to be available again, helping the 13 personnel passing game.
signals.note: His return restores a vertical-threat tight end, which could cut into the targets and snaps of the other tight ends.
signals.quote: Good to see him moving around

signals.note: He is on the injury report and the coach framed his impact as conditional on health, with Ferguson now returning.
signals.quote: Colby Parkinson when he's been healthy has made a huge impact for us

signals.note: The coach praised his consistency, but his share of snaps could shrink as Ferguson and Parkinson get healthy.

signals.claim: Atwell will be targeted more going forward, though how the ball is distributed is decided week to week.
signals.note: The coach confirmed the team wants to get him the ball more after his key conversion plays and two-minute drive. Volume is not guaranteed.

signals.claim: Nacua stays the offense's primary playmaker and the receiver Matthew Stafford trusts most in key moments.
signals.note: With Adams out, he is the clear top option and can be used deep, underneath and in the run game.
signals.quote: he finds a way to make plays over and over again

signals.claim: Nacua is still explosive despite the earlier hip and calf injuries.
signals.note: The coach downplayed the earlier injuries, but the report lists a DNP with a knee issue that he did not address.
signals.quote: I've still seen a guy that's been able to be, um, you know, explosive

signals.claim: Whittington will get snaps as a supplementary receiver with Adams out, contributing through blocking and jet sweeps as much as catches.
signals.note: He and the other depth receivers have combined for only two catches in the past two weeks, so the role may not bring much fantasy production.
signals.quote: we have guys that we feel that we can put, you know, trust in

signals.claim: Mumpfield will get snaps as a supplementary receiver with Adams out, contributing through blocking and jet sweeps as much as catches.
signals.note: He is a depth receiver whose role is described mainly in terms of blocking and gadget plays, not catch volume.
signals.quote: we have guys that we feel that we can put, you know, trust in

topics.detail: Scheelhaase said the offense finds its rhythm quickly in tempo and chaotic situations because the players have continuity and clarity about where everyone should be. He called it something to build on.

He stressed that blocking in the run game and jet sweep handoffs are big parts of the offense and do not show up in the box score. He expects the receivers to be asked to do a lot in a 60-70 play game.
Scheelhaase praised Donald's daily mentality and the stories about his approach around the building. He cited a Sean McVay story about 'controlled aggression.'

title: OC Bobby Slowik - Nov 5 | Press Conference
headline: Slowik says the run game needs its aggression back against Detroit, Malik Willis left some scramble chances on the field, and Kaytron Allen is still only 'progressing' toward offensive snaps.
summary: Slowik said he doesn't plan to change the offense's tempo, because going up tempo shrinks the play menu and makes the offense predictable. He defended the slow pace in the late-game drive, saying that down 10 or 11 with six minutes left is not yet panic time. He said last week was the first game this season where the run blocking fell short, and that New England's varied looks plus a lack of conviction hurt the run game. He wants that mentality back, and says practice so far has been encouraging. He called spreading targets around healthy and wants fewer three-and-outs and more consistency. He said Malik Willis left some run opportunities on the field, which is easier to see on film than live, and that they are training him on it. He praised Kadyn Proctor's impact and said Jarrett Kingston settled in after a slow start while filling in for him. He previewed a tough Lions front (Hutchinson and the interior rushers) and said the tackles will get help from slides, screens, quick throws and runs. On Kaytron Allen, he praised his two special teams plays but offered no timeline for offensive snaps.

injuries.detail: Was unavailable last game and Slowik did not say whether he returns this week. He is not on the provided injury report.
Full practice participant (quadricep) on the injury report. Slowik said he is progressing but gave no timeline for offensive snaps.

signals.claim: Willis is being coached to recognize and take scramble/run opportunities that he passed up last game.
signals.note: Possible rushing upside for Willis if he starts converting those open windows, but Slowik framed it as work in progress.
signals.quote: we had some ups last week that we kind of left out there

signals.note: Slowik stressed how much Proctor helps the run game and explosive plays, so his availability matters for the offense's efficiency.
signals.quote: you can feel Proctor's presence on most every play

signals.claim: Kingston filled in for Proctor and improved as the game went on, especially in the second half.
signals.note: Offensive line stability affects the run game and Willis; Kingston's second-half improvement is a mildly good sign if Proctor stays out.
signals.quote: I thought he kind of fell into a rhythm

signals.claim: Allen is progressing but is not yet confirmed to contribute from scrimmage.
signals.note: Two big special teams plays could earn him offensive carries eventually, but there is no timeline, so he is only a stash-level watch.
signals.quote: I would just say he's he's progressing.

topics.detail: Slowik doesn't expect to drastically change the tempo. He says going up tempo narrows the play menu and can backfire when defenses show unexpected looks. He defended the deliberate drive late, saying the goal at six minutes left, down 10 or 11, was simply to get points.

Slowik said the run game needs to return to the conviction and aggression of earlier weeks, after New England varied its looks. He thinks the offense blocked well overall this season but not last week. He said practice has been encouraging so far this week.
He likes that many receivers are getting targets, because it makes the offense harder to defend. He wants fewer three-and-outs and more consistent execution and play calling.

He said Detroit's defense has been much improved over the last three weeks. He called its front, including Aidan Hutchinson and the interior rushers, a major test of the offense's physicality. The plan is to help the tackles with slides, screens, quick throws and runs.
He described the deflected interception as a fluke, since Willis was hit in the back as he released the ball. He said Willis is handling it well.

title: Kubiak, Morris Preview Raiders, Talk Buckner’s Return to the Fold
headline: Demarcus Robinson is back at practice for SF and Kubiak says he hasn't missed a beat; the staff is also weighing a receiver trade before the deadline.
summary: Klay Kubiak opened with his brother's Raiders matchup, calling it a blessing to share a field with a sibling. He added that working on the same staff in 2023 was a unique experience he'd love to repeat. He praised Trent Williams at length, calling him still the best offensive lineman in the league and crediting his weekly preparation. Asked about the trade deadline, he said the staff weighs the room's needs and depth, who is returning from injury, and whether the young receivers are worth keeping on their development track. He also noted that new receivers are hard to plug in quickly. He said the staff evaluates every position, that the outcome is out of his control, and that they may simply stay with what they have. On Demarcus Robinson, he said it's great to have him back, that he's practicing well, and that he's quickly rebuilding timing with the quarterback after a long absence. The rest of the video is defensive coordinator Raheem Morris on DeForest Buckner, the secondary and Brock Bowers, which is not Kubiak's commentary.

injuries.detail: Back at practice after being out a while; Kubiak says he's practicing well and getting his timing back. He was a full participant on the injury report (ankle).

signals.claim: Robinson has returned to practice and is already back up to speed in the offense.
signals.note: A healthy Robinson restores a receiver option and could take snaps and targets from the other wideouts.
signals.quote: He's jumped right back in there. And like he hasn't missed a beat.

signals.claim: Williams is still playing at an elite level at age 38.
signals.note: Williams' continued strong play supports the pass protection and run game for the 49ers' skill players, though he did not practice this week (listed as resting).
signals.quote: He's to me, he's still the best offensive lineman in the league

topics.detail: Kubiak said the staff weighs room depth, injury returns and young-player development before adding a receiver. He noted that a newcomer would struggle to learn the offense quickly and said they may stay with what they have. The decision is out of his hands.

Kubiak treats facing his brother's team as a blessing and says the game is just another one to compete in. He called the 2023 season on the same staff, which included a Super Bowl run, a great experience.

The second half of the video is Morris discussing Buckner's return, Bosa trending in the right direction, cornerback depth including Upton Stout, and the challenge of covering Raiders TE Brock Bowers.
